stem: A company has 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Employees sign in with user accounts in an Active Directory domain in the company's data center. The data center already connects to a VPC through AWS Direct Connect. The employees must use their existing Active Directory credentials to access the AWS accounts. The company does not want to run domain controllers in AWS or to keep copies of the users or passwords in AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: does not want to run domain controllers in AWS

options.text: Configure SAML 2.0 federation from an AD FS server in the data center to an IAM identity provider and IAM roles in each AWS account.
options.why: It works, but you [federate workforce users through your identity provider to specific AWS accounts](../facts/iam.md#iam-federation-with-iam-per-account-saml-or-oidc), so each account needs its own provider and roles.
options.misconception: federates each account separately when one central sign-in service exists

options.text: Create IAM users in each AWS account with a script that copies the user names from Active Directory, and require MFA for each IAM user.
options.why: Employees get new passwords, because [IAM users have long-term credentials such as passwords and access keys](../facts/iam.md#iam-users-have-long-term-credentials-roles-do-not), so the Active Directory credentials stay unused.

options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, and create a trust relationship with the on-premises domain.
options.why: It runs [a highly available pair of domain controllers](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-managed-ad-dc-pair-across-azs) in AWS, but AD Connector works [without caching any information in the cloud](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-on-premises-ad-two-options).

options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector as the identity source, and assign permission sets to Active Directory groups for the AWS accounts.
options.why: AD Connector is a directory gateway that works [without caching any information in the cloud](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-on-premises-ad-two-options), and permission sets give each group its access.

explanation: IAM Identity Center manages access to [multiple AWS accounts, AWS applications, and other SAML-enabled cloud applications](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-built-on-iam-for-multi-account-access), and it [applies these permissions to the selected accounts automatically](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-permission-sets). An on-premises domain connects through AD Connector, which works [without caching any information in the cloud](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-on-premises-ad-two-options). Its VPC reaches the data center through a [(VPN) connection or Direct Connect](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-needs-vpn-or-direct-connect), and the stem gives that link. Employees keep their Active Directory credentials, and no domain controllers run in AWS.
takeaway: Employees in an on-premises Active Directory reach many accounts through IAM Identity Center with AD Connector.
twin: If the stem said "employees sign in with Okta Universal Directory" instead: connect Okta as the identity source, because IAM Identity Center supports [Microsoft Active Directory, Okta Universal Directory, Microsoft Entra ID](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-identity-sources).
say: Use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector, so employees keep their AD passwords and no directory runs in AWS.

solvers.stem_only: Use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector as the identity source: AD Connector proxies authentication to the on-premises AD with no directory or password copies in AWS; assign permission sets to AD groups across the 40 accounts.

solvers.flag: Missing constraint: AD Connector needs the VPC connected to the data center through a VPN connection or Direct Connect (directory-service-ad-connector-needs-vpn-or-direct-connect); the stem does not say this connection exists, so a reader could argue the AD FS SAML option has less setup; add one sentence that the data center already connects to AWS through a VPN or Direct Connect.
citations: docs/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/what_is#AD Connector also eliminates the need of

solvers.flag: A careful candidate could argue that AD Connector is itself a directory in AWS Directory Service (it has a directory ID and is listed as a directory type), so the constraint 'does not want to run a second directory in AWS' could be read to exclude it and push toward the AD FS SAML federation option, which also needs no password copies; consider rewording the constraint as 'does not want to copy or synchronize the users or passwords into AWS'.
